title: The Bear and the Garden Lover
text:
A bear lived alone in the mountains, and after a while solitude began to depress him. Not far away lived an old man who loved his garden but was lonely too, since flowers make poor conversation. One morning the two met on a path. Nervous as he was, the old man invited the bear to his home, and soon they were fast friends.

They suited each other well. The bear said little and spent his days hunting, bringing game home for them both. His chief task, as he saw it, was to keep the flies off his friend while the old man slept.

One day, as the old man was sound asleep, a fly landed on the tip of his nose. The bear chased it away, but it came back. He chased it again, and again it landed. The bear grew angry. "I will get you this time," he thought. He picked up a heavy paving stone and hurled it with all his strength.

He killed the fly. He also crushed his friend's skull.

La Fontaine ends: nothing is as dangerous as an ignorant friend. A wise enemy would be better.
lesson: Good intentions are not enough; help must be fitted to the real need. Be wary of zealous helpers who lack judgment, and check that your own help does not do harm.
source: Jean de La Fontaine, Fables, Book VIII, Fable 10
